answer: The Sybil defence is per-identity capital bonding: an agent locks a bond scaling with the influence it seeks before voting or claiming payouts. A Sybil farm then pays that bond per clone, so cost grows with farm size instead of staying flat, and a clone caught colluding forfeits its bond to honest participants, making the raid loss-making. Reputation is the second wall, a forge where only slow verified work raises limits, so fresh aliases start at zero and each needs costly history to reach the garden of trusted seats. A staking pulse with slashing for duplicate proofs ejects clone farms.
